sources.notes:
Poland's post-study job-search permit: NINE MONTHS, granted ONCE, and it must be applied for DIRECTLY AFTER graduation. The page states 'Zezwolenie na pobyt czasowy udzielane jest jednorazowo, bezposrednio po zakonczeniu studiow na okres 9 miesiecy' - granted once, immediately after finishing studies, for 9 months.

BACHELOR LEVEL IS EXPLICITLY COVERED. The eligibility text reads 'Cudzoziemcowi, ktory jest absolwentem polskiej uczelni' - a foreigner who is a graduate of a Polish higher education institution. It does not restrict to Master's, and the supporting document required is 'dyplom ukonczenia polskiej uczelni' without level restriction. So unlike Sweden's second-cycle-only permit, Poland's is open at Bachelor's.

TWO CONDITIONS WORTH FLAGGING FOR A FIRST-YEAR MODEL, both on this page. First, the nine months cannot be banked: the application must go in 'nie pozniej niz w ostatnim dniu jego legalnego pobytu', i.e. no later than the last day of lawful stay, so a student who defers has no deferred job-search window. Second, a proof of an arranged place of residence in Poland is required even though the permit is for job hunting.

FINANCIAL THRESHOLD, recorded because the brief's financial-proof topic needs it and this page carries a specific Polish figure. The monthly funds must exceed the social-assistance income threshold: 'powinna przekraczac 823zl dla osob w rodzinie lub 1010 zl dla osob samotnie gospodarujacych'. Note the direction is EXCEED, not 'at least', so PLN 823/PLN 1,010 are floors to clear, not the required amounts. The underlying amounts are defined by the 2004 social assistance statute rather than set on this page.

The figure is attributed to one provincial office page (Podlaskie). I did not fetch a second voivodeship office or the UDSC central page, so while gov.pl is the authoritative national portal, I record this as a single-office statement of the national rule. Note also that the udsc page I fetched returned navigation only with no article body, so I could not corroborate there.

LEGAL BASIS, quoted: 'Art. 186 ust. 1 pkt 6 ustawy z dnia 12 grudnia 2013 r. o cudzoziemcach'. Recorded so the corpus can point at the statute.

sources.notes:
Poland's student-residence financial proof, stated in a form that is directly usable. Base monthly amount: PLN 1,010 for a person living alone, PLN 823 for a person living in a family. Critically, the base figure is NOT the total: the page says the base is 'plus rental and utility fees for each month of stay'. Any Polish cost model that uses PLN 1,010 as the total monthly requirement will understate it by the whole rent and utilities.

HORIZON IS 15 MONTHS, which is unusual and easy to miss: 'for the period of 15 months of stay or for the whole period of stay in Poland, when your stay will be shorter than 15 months'. So the first-year proof is fifteen months of base plus rent, not twelve. Separately, the page notes a third-country return-travel requirement of PLN 2,500, PLN 500 for a non-neighbouring EU citizen, and PLN 200 for a neighbour.

The page's own worked example is quoted verbatim and is the clearest single illustration of how the components combine: a person from China renting at PLN 900 all-inclusive 'must have PLN 1910 for each month of planned stay in Poland + PLN 2500 for a return ticket to your country + money to cover tuition fees for the rest of your studies.' PLN 1,010 + PLN 900 = PLN 1,910, which is the page doing the addition itself, so I do not rely on my own arithmetic.

ACCEPTABLE PROOF DOCUMENTS, and one of them matters for a scholarship corpus: 'certificate of awarding the scholarship' is an accepted instrument. Also credit card limit certificate, a Polish bank account certificate, and an employment and earnings certificate.

TIMING CONSTRAINT: certificates must be issued no earlier than one month before submission.

PROVENANCE CAVEAT, stated rather than hidden. This is a university page, and the priority for this metric is the national authority. It is credible and detailed but it is a university's guidance, not the regulation. I attempted two national sources: the Podlaskie provincial office graduate page (fetched successfully, and it carries the same PLN 823 / PLN 1,010 thresholds for the GRADUATE permit, recorded in 002_post_study_work.json) and the Lublin and Lower Silesian provincial office student-permit pages, both of which returned transport errors, plus the UDSC central page which returned navigation with no article body. The underlying regulation is a 2022 Minister of the Interior ordinance on the amount of financial resources a foreigner undertaking studies must hold; I saw it referenced in search results but did not fetch a readable copy, so I do not quote its figures.

WHAT I DID NOT ESTABLISH: the exact PLN amount that the ordinance itself sets, and any 2026 update to the PLN 823 / PLN 1,010 thresholds. The university's page carries no explicit 'as of' year on the figures, so as_of is recorded conservatively.

sources.notes:
Bachelor tuition at a named public Polish university. The Faculty of Management, University of Warsaw, English-language Bachelor's programme 'Business and Management' is 'Paid studies' with tuition for 2026/2027 of 4 000 EUR for one instalment covering the academic year, or 2 200 EUR for each of two instalments for the academic year, or four instalments of 1 200 EUR. The page header states 'Bachelor's studies (Full-time studies)' and 'Duration: 3 years/6 semesters', so this is unambiguously a Bachelor's figure.

PER ACADEMIC YEAR, NOT PER SEMESTER. The page's own headings attach the amounts to 'for the academic year'. Two instalments at 2 200 EUR each equals the 4 000 EUR single-instalment figure, which is internally consistent and confirms the annual reading. The earlier search-engine snippet for this programme rendered the figure as '4 000 EUR/semester', which would be wrong by a factor of two; the fetched page is the authority and it says per academic year. That discrepancy is worth flagging because a search index is exactly where a doubled tuition figure would enter a corpus unchecked.

The university also charges a PLN 22 student ID (legitymacja) payment, recorded verbatim on the same page.

COVERAGE LIMIT, stated rather than glossed. This is one faculty at one university. Poland does not have a single national Bachelor tuition figure: it is set per programme by each institution. The University of Warsaw's central admissions office publishes a per-faculty fee schedule as a PDF, and I attempted to fetch two of those PDFs (rekrutacja.uw.edu.pl/files/pdf/tuition_fees_2026-2027_05.10.2026.pdf and the WNE faculty fee declaration). Both returned raw PDF binary streams that this tool could not decode into readable text, so I could not quote them. Their existence is visible from the university pages I did fetch, but I do not record any figure from them. Other faculties at the same university carry different fees, and the WNE faculty fee declaration surfaced in search results showing figures such as 4 900 EUR per year for its business programmes, which is consistent with per-faculty variation, but I did not fetch a page I could read and so I do not record it.

A separate official university page, the Welcome Point tuition-fees page, confirms the mechanism in prose I did read verbatim: 'Tuition fees differ depending on the terms of admission, the language of studies, and the year of admission.' That sentence is the reason a single Polish national figure cannot be asserted, and it is why this file carries a named-university figure only.
